change_description: EXISTING BUG: backtest.py:654 prior_season_pitcher_fi uses sitCodes=[i1] which returns zero splits from the MLB Stats API statSplits endpoint; correct code is sitCodes=[i01]. Function has been silently falling back to the no-FI-data default branch since commit a82677a (2026-04-25 'Add LR-v1 model, dashboard, backtest infrastructure'), ~17 days. DEFERRED -- isolate fix in its own PR after Phase 2.1 ships or rolls back, so Phase 2.1 gates don't conflate two changes.
notes: Verified 2026-05-12 via read-only API calls: sitCodes=[i01] returns expected first-inning splits for Skubal 2025 (31.0 IP / 1.45 ERA), Webb 2025 (34.0 IP / 3.71 ERA), Cole 2023 (33.0 IP / 2.73 ERA). sitCodes=[i1] returns zero splits for all three. Repro one-liner: statsapi.get('person', {'personId': 543037, 'hydrate': 'stats(group=[pitching],type=[statSplits],sitCodes=[i01],season=2023)'})  vs  the same with sitCodes=[i1]. Impact estimate: fi_pitcher blend in mlb_first_inning_predictor.py:827 has been receiving zero FI samples and never triggering, so the lineup is currently relying purely on full-season ERA blends. Real-world effect unclear -- model may already be partly compensating via other features.

change_description: EXISTING BUG: LEAGUE_FIRST_INNING_RUNS = 0.475 hardcoded in mlb_first_inning_predictor.py line 75 is ~7% understated vs 2024+2025 empirical mean of 0.510 runs per first half-inning (4802 game-half-innings sampled from data/backtests/backtest_2024-*_truepit.csv and backtest_2025-*_truepit.csv). Affects lambda computation in the predictor, which in turn gates STRONG YRFI via LAMBDA_YRFI_FLOOR = 0.78. Likely cause of suppressed STRONG YRFI rate. DO NOT FIX in Phase 2.1 -- changing this constant during 2.1 backfill/training would conflate gate results across two changes. Isolated PR after 2.1 ships or rolls back.
notes: Discovered 2026-05-12 during Phase 2.1 Q3 empirical FI ERA verification. Year-by-year: 2024 = 0.489 runs/half (4.40 FI 'ERA' on total runs, ~4.22 earned-only), 2025 = 0.532 runs/half (4.79 / ~4.60). The 0.475 constant appears to be a pre-pitch-clock (pre-2023) estimate that did not get refreshed when pitch clock pushed offense up. Year-over-year delta of +0.39 ERA between 2024 and 2025 is itself a separate finding -- see Phase 2.1 month-by-month diagnostic on the same date.

change_description: BUG: tools/backfill_pitcher_ids.py overwrites data/diagnostics/pid_resolution_mismatches.csv on each run instead of merging. Loses prior-run mismatches: 2024 PID backfill produced 47 mismatches, then 2025 PID backfill overwrote the file with its 35 mismatches, dropping the 2024 record from disk. Fix: read existing diagnostics CSV at script start, append new mismatches, dedupe on (date, game_pk, side, source_file), atomic write. DO NOT FIX in Phase 2.1 -- isolated PR after Phase 2.1 ships or rolls back, same pattern as the other two deferred bugs (i1 and LEAGUE_FIRST_INNING_RUNS). Workaround applied 2026-05-13: re-ran the resolver in dry-run mode with both --file args so the in-memory accumulation produces a combined 82-row diagnostics file on a single write. CSV name columns were never overwritten by the PID backfill so the mismatch detection is deterministic on re-runs.
notes: Workaround verified 2026-05-13: combined file shows 47 rows from backtest_2024-*_truepit.csv + 35 rows from backtest_2025-*_truepit.csv = 82 rows total. Both source files represented. Existing 2024 + 2025 CSVs already have PID columns populated from the prior live runs; this dry-run touched no CSV data, only the diagnostics file.

change_description: BUG: Phase 2.1 train-time fallback for blank home/away_first_inning_era cells uses LEAGUE_AVG_ERA = 4.20 (full-season, not FI-specific) via two_stage_model.py gather()'s coerce default. Not fixed in V1 per explicit operator decision -- <1% impact, train/predict semantics diverge only on the rare 47-postponement-row slots which contain no real pitcher signal anyway. Fix in V1.1 alongside any other gather() refactor (e.g. when adding current-season-to-date FI per V1.1 design).

change_description: BUG: two_stage_model.py line 694's post-training 'user scenario test' hardcodes a 13-feature vector and crashes with ValueError shape mismatch when trained model has any other feature count. Training itself completes successfully (weights saved at line 508 before the crash). Affects all phase variants except whichever historical 13-feature variant the test was written for. Non-blocking but visible to operator as a confusing traceback after successful training. Fix: either remove the scenario test, or parameterize it to match the actual trained feature count.
notes: Deleted lines 660-702 of two_stage_model.py -- scenario test was hardcoded to 13-feature phase-e3 (stale since Phase F upgraded to 18 features).  Per Claude Code analysis, try/except wrap would have created skip-noise on every run; clean delete is correct. Resolution verified 2026-05-13 by re-running V2.3-fie training -- exits rc=0 with same Brier (0.2442) as before the crash.  Same crash signature also blocked Gate A via candidate_validation.py; both unblocked by this fix.

change_description: Phase 2.2 -- pitcher first-pitch strike % in 1st inning.  Bayesian-blended FPS_1st per pitcher, shrunk to single league prior LEAGUE_FPS_1ST_AVG=0.62 (empirically 0.6194 across 92547 events 2021-2026) with N_PRIOR_FPS=20 events.  Adds home_first_pitch_strike_pct to T1 and away_first_pitch_strike_pct to B1 (19 features per half total vs phase-e3's 18).  Per-pitch Statcast pull via pybaseball; year-stable post-pitch-clock environment so no year-indexing needed (unlike Phase 2.1 FIE).  Single-source-of-truth import of LEAGUE_FPS_1ST_AVG eliminates train/predict divergence risk that FIE has.  Trained candidate at data/candidates/v23_fps/ on 2026-05-14.
gate_result: FAIL -- 2/3 splits favored candidate (gate 1 PASS) but S3 delta -0.0001 vs threshold -0.003 (gate 2 FAIL, 30x below).  Distinct from FIE's pattern: FIE had 1/3 wins (S1/S2 exactly 0.0000); FPS has 2/3 wins (real-signed negative deltas on S2+S3).  Filed as FAIL per playbook (the threshold is the threshold) but mechanistically different.
notes: Feature has real signal -- 2-of-3 splits favored candidate -- but signal magnitude is too small to clear the -0.003 S3 gate.  Coefficient magnitudes (T1=-0.0190, B1=-0.0173, both signed correctly negative since higher FPS -> fewer runs allowed) survive the existing 18-feature stack and produce the most symmetric pitcher-quality feature in the model (T1/B1 ratio 1.10x, vs FIP 12x, xERA 16x, FIE 2x).  Marginal Brier contribution is ~0.0001, not 0.003.  Pre-Gate-A diagnostics ALL pointed at a real feature (Q5 mean |delta| 4.3pp, stddev 5.2pp; named-pitcher archetypes mapping correctly; deGrom topping the league at 0.7121; Brady Basso bottoming at 0.4391).  The trained model IS using FPS -- it's just not enough to move the meta-aggregate Brier by 30bp.  Mild whiff_pct_rank absorption (~7-8% shift more negative) suggests FPS captures something correlated-but-not-identical to whiff-based count leverage.  Per playbook 'Common Pitfalls #2', FPS is shelved without iteration.  No L2 sweep, no prior adjustment, no current-season-to-date refinement.  This row is distinct from FIE: if a future feature interacts favorably with FPS (e.g. a count-leverage feature that's orthogonal to whiff and FPS both), this is the row to revisit.  More broadly, this is information about how close to optimal V2.2 already is on the existing data sources -- a feature that 'should' help based on Q5-style pre-diagnostics, trains with meaningful coefficients, passes named-pitcher smell tests, can still fail to clear a 0.003 Brier gate.  Trained weights left at data/candidates/v23_fps/ for reproducibility.  Phase 2.2 closed 2026-05-14.  Next: Phase 2.3 leadoff hitter isolation (per playbook ordering).

change_description: Phase 2.1 -- pitcher first-inning ERA feature.  Bayesian-blended FI ERA per pitcher, shrunk to year-indexed LEAGUE_FI_AVG_ERA_BY_TARGET_SEASON with N_PRIOR_FI=30 IP.  Adds home_first_inning_era to T1 and away_first_inning_era to B1 (19 features per half total vs phase-e3's 18).  Trained candidate at data/candidates/v23_fie/ on 2026-05-13.
gate_result: FAIL -- S3 delta -0.0001 vs threshold -0.003 (30x below). Feature redundant with existing FIP/xERA/last5/last10/pvt signals per pre-Gate-A weight analysis. Shelved.
notes: Gate A failed both criteria. All three splits returned TIE (deltas within +/-0.0001).  Mechanistically the pre-Gate-A weight inspection foretold this: trained FIE coefficients were tiny (T1=+0.0069, B1=+0.0035, signed correctly) vs xera ~0.04 and top3c_iso ~0.4.  The FIE T1/B1 asymmetry was ~2x, MILDER than FIP (~12x) or xERA (~16x), indicating FIE carries comparatively uniform signal across halves -- but that uniform signal is small in absolute terms.  Interpretation: the pitcher's first-inning-specific ERA, when shrunk via Bayesian blend and added alongside FIP+xERA+last5_nrfi+last10_nrfi+pvt_nrfi (5 existing pitcher-quality features), provides essentially no marginal signal beyond what's already captured.  Per playbook 'Common Pitfalls #2 -- p-hacking the feature definition', FIE is shelved without iteration.  No L2 sweep, no lookback adjustment, no current-season-to-date V1.1 attempt -- if the V1 feature design produces zero marginal Brier signal across 3 splits with sample N=4802, the answer is not 'try a different definition' but 'this feature is captured by existing signals'.  Trained weights left on disk at data/candidates/v23_fie/ for reproducibility.  Phase 2.1 closed 2026-05-13.  Next: Phase 2.2 first-pitch strike percentage (per playbook ordering).

change_description: 2024 deep_nrfi bucket miscalibrated +11.77pp (n=170) -- STRONG NRFI bets in 2024 backtest were ~12pp overconfident vs empirical (model mean 65.29%, actual NRFI rate 53.53%).  Drops to +2.53pp in 2025 (n=220, model 65.71% vs actual 63.18%) and +0.51pp in 2026 (n=11, model 64.14% vs actual 63.64%).  This is historical environment drift (pitch-clock era), not active leak.  Calibrator has caught up.  No action needed, documented for institutional memory.  If a future analysis asks 'why does V2.3 backtest worse on 2024 than 2025-2026?', this is the explanation.
notes: Identified 2026-05-14 during Phase 2.3 vs Phase 3.2 read-only pivot investigation.  Fresh-run analysis of current LR weights + current calibration_v2.json against backtest_2024-*_truepit.csv (N=2409 graded) bucketed by calibrated nrfi_prob.  calibration_v2.json was fit on 2025+2026 combined (train_n=2927) so by construction is well-calibrated on those years but allowed to drift on 2024 -- which is exactly what we see.  Largest miscal across the bucket grid; no other bucket shows >5pp miss after 2024.  Implication for future feature work: candidate_validation.py S2 (train 2025, test 2024) will systematically under-credit features that help NRFI predictions in the deep_nrfi zone, since the baseline already over-predicts there.  Phase 2.1 FIE S2 TIE (+0.0000) and Phase 2.2 FPS S2 TIE (-0.0001) are consistent with that, though deltas leave no room for confident attribution.

change_description: Phase 2.3 backfill uses fetch_top3_batters which prefers post-game boxscore.battingOrder (actual lineup) and falls back to schedule.lineups (announced lineup).  Production at predict-time hits schedule.lineups first (boxscore empty pre-pitch).  ~5% of slots differ across the two sources due to late scratches.  NOT a stat-level leak -- both sources get strict-less-than date stat cutoffs at backtest.py:1501 (relevant = [g for g in log if g['date'] < target_date_iso]).  Estimated training-signal effect ~0.1pp from 0.05 * 7pp * 1/3, inside noise of natural OBP variance.  Accepted deliberately: training on actual batting order correctly attributes 1st-inning labels to the batters who created them; predict-time announced lineup is the best available estimate.  Documented for institutional memory.
notes: Identified 2026-05-14 during Phase 2.3 pre-backfill leakage review.  The hard-gate leakage check (per-batter stat cutoff) PASSED -- this finding is the separate, smaller composition asymmetry that surfaced while reading the source.  Alternative would be reordering fetch_top3_batters to query schedule.lineups first, but the MLB Stats API likely doesn't retain historical announced lineups for closed seasons, so strict prod-time semantics may not be achievable for backfill anyway.  Train/serve consistency framing: the backfill teaches the model 'this batter at this prior-stat level correlates with NRFI', and production at predict-time provides the announced-batter's prior stats as the best available proxy.  Both sides see prior-only data.  If a future analysis asks 'why does V2.3 train Brier look slightly better than walk-forward Brier?', this asymmetry is a candidate explanation worth examining.

change_description: BUG: tools/candidate_validation.py overwrites trained weights (lr_t1.json + lr_b1.json) and now (post-Gate-C-plumbing) rowwise CSVs in an existing --candidate directory without confirmation or backup.  Risk: a reference candidate dir kept for reproducibility (e.g. data/candidates/v23_fie/, v23_fps/) gets silently clobbered by an unrelated run.  Same risk for --baseline-tmp.  Fix options: (a) prompt for confirmation if --candidate dir already contains lr_t1.json; (b) add --force flag and refuse-by-default when dir exists; (c) auto-archive existing weights to a timestamped sibling before overwriting.  Defer -- not blocking Phase 2.3 since the trained-weight dirs are recreated by every Gate A run anyway, and the only kept-for-reference dirs (v23_fie, v23_fps) live at distinct candidate paths not in scope for Phase 2.3.
notes: Filed 2026-05-14.  Concrete trigger: during Phase 2.3 backfill design review, the operator asked 'does candidate_validation.py crash if you build the parser?' -- to answer, the assistant ran a full Gate A invocation (--phase-e3 --fps) that overwrote data/candidates/.baseline_tmp/lr_t1.json + lr_b1.json.  No production data harm (baseline_tmp is by design a scratch dir), but it surfaced the systemic gap: nothing in the script prevents that overwrite even on a real candidate dir.  Operator's process note also logged: 'smallest test that answers the question' -- here the answer was achievable via `python -c 'import candidate_validation'` or an invocation with a bad flag, no full Gate A needed.

change_description: BUG: tools/candidate_validation.py --fps help text contains a bare '%' (the string 'first-pitch strike % in 1st inning') that crashes argparse's --help formatter with TypeError ('%i format: a real number is required, not dict').  argparse's _expand_help applies %-substitution to help strings using a params dict; the bare '%' followed by ' in' is interpreted as a partial format spec.  Introduced 2026-05-14 when Phase 2.2 --fps flag was added.  COSMETIC ONLY -- does not affect non-help invocations.  argparse builds the parser at module import time; _format_help / _expand_help only run when --help is invoked.  Verified by running 'python tools/candidate_validation.py --phase-e3 --fps --candidate /tmp/x' which built the parser and proceeded normally into a Gate A pass.  One-character fix: '%' -> '%%' in the help string (argparse strips the escape during expansion).  Defer -- not blocking Phase 2.3.
notes: Same isolation rule as other deferred bugs: fix in own commit after Phase 2.3 closes.  Note that two_stage_model.py uses '%%' correctly in its own --clean-only help (line 527: '~22%% of historical'), so the pattern is already known in the codebase -- this was just an oversight when Phase 2.2 was added to the validator.
